review_method: Independent visual inspection of retained original regional, river-line and station maps and every complete selected baseline path; independent decoding compares exact selected IDs, fragment order, every position and all metadata with immutable baseline inputs. Public validation checks included summaries and factual linkage only.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory target IDs, not individual named rivers or verified reach names.

inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete eastern basin corresponds at regional scale to water beneath the Lake part of the Sandfly Lake label. Its broad northern cap, western notch, eastern indentation and lower eastward arm taper into the southern tip. The full outline was compared with mapped water and surrounding shore. This supports generalized Sandfly Lake association for the selected feature, not equivalence with the entire named lake or extension of that name to connecting river water.

The entire north-south outline corresponds geographically to mapped water between Struga, Ohrid and Pogradec. Its broad northern cap, northeast shoulder, long east and west sides and rounded southern end were compared. Lake Ohrid is a low-confidence geographic naming candidate from literal wording within a partial conservation overlay, qualified by re-designate. Strong shape correspondence does not establish name coverage or naming authority for the complete selected water polygon. No supported whole-water identity or protected-site/water-boundary equivalence is assigned.

findings.supported_name_scope: Both selected fragments were viewed in full: a southwestern upper course curves east and north into a high northern bend, then the lower path turns southeast and northeast toward the coast. The direct blue Clarence label on the mapped lower/eastern river line supports Clarence River as the representative system identity. The long western and southwestern feeder course is not individually named; nearby Boyd wording does not establish its exact name partition. Both fragments carry modeled mainstem roles, which do not make every part Clarence. Coastal and feeder-to-main-river transitions remain unassigned at reach level.
limits: The direct blue Clarence river-line label is identity evidence; the black Clarence River catchment leader alone is not.
Western and southwestern upper feeder names and their transitions remain unverified; nearby Boyd wording is not promoted to a reach assignment.
The original publication is a coarse regional assessment, not a formal naming-register decision or surveyed contemporary mouth map.
Original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality and exact source reach-to-rendered-part name mapping are not verified.

findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path starts on a far-western feeder, turns north and east through the western Goulburn corridor, and continues southeast along the lower Hunter through the Singleton, Greta and Maitland area toward Newcastle. The mapped Hunter River at Greta station and direct Hunter line label support Hunter River as a representative system identity. Figure 4.46 separately labels Goulburn and Munmurra along the western corridor, so this modeled mainstem is not uniformly Hunter. These are regional channel associations, not exact source-reach assignments. Feeder junctions, storage-related boundaries and the coastal ending remain unassigned at reach level; the northeastern Glenbawn/Pages branch is not the selected upper path.
limits: The mapped Hunter River at Greta station and Hunter river-line label anchor the name; the Hunter catchment title alone does not.
Separately mapped Goulburn and Munmurra show a naming distinction within the western corridor; exact part boundaries and a uniform Hunter name are not established.
Glenbawn, Lake St Clair and Lostock are basin storage context. Their presence does not place all these storages on the selected path.

findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path runs north from the southern inland headwater, bends northeast and north through the interior, then turns east across the Tallowa vicinity toward the coast. Direct blue Shoalhaven river-line wording, the mapped storage location and explicit text placing Tallowa on the Shoalhaven River support Shoalhaven River as a representative system identity. The southern headwater or feeder nomenclature, exact river/storage transitions and coastal ending remain individually unassigned. The modeled mainstem role does not establish a uniform name for every part or name the storage water separately.
limits: The direct blue Shoalhaven river-line label and Tallowa-on-river text support the association; catchment and storage names alone do not.
Tallowa is storage context, not an exact river-reservoir boundary or permission to apply Shoalhaven to every southern feeder or coastal segment.
